subject: INLA dealing with anisotropy geostatistical data?

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: INLA dealing with anisotropy geostatistical data?
parts:
Hi INLA groups,

I wonder whether INLA with SPDE can handle anisotropy geostatistical data?
If INLA can handle snisotropy data, whether there are some tutorials or reproducible R-INLA code?

Indeed, I found that my spatial data are anisotropic. 
However, in Cameletti's case, the spatial data is isotropic. Moreover, it seems that barrier model is not adaptive to my case.

Many thanks

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA dealing with anisotropy geostatistical data?
parts:
Neo,

Do you have spatial replicates?

Do you want space-varying anisotropy, or constant?

Can you provide your evidence that your data is anisotropic?

There is no trivial ways to do anisotropy in INLA, but depending on the above we can guide you to a suggested approach.

PS: One of the reasons some of the more complex non-stationary models are not fully implemented is that we are waiting for a really good dataset motivation.

Kind regards,
Haakon
